summary: Shows the output of encrypt_string with a vault ID (header $ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.2;AES256;dev) and how to encrypt a value piped on stdin with --stdin-name, warning that secrets typed on the command line end up in shell history.
questions: How do I pipe a secret into ansible-vault encrypt_string?
Does a vault ID show up in the encrypted output?
Is it safe to type the secret on the command line?

answer_card.title: Encrypt a string from stdin
answer_card.answer_md:
With a vault ID, the header includes the label: `$ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.2;AES256;dev`.

To read the value from stdin:

```bash
echo -n 'letmein' | ansible-vault encrypt_string --vault-id dev@a_password_file --stdin-name 'db_password'
```

Output:

```yaml
db_password: !vault |
          $ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.2;AES256;dev
          6132393135...
```

**Warning**: typing the secret directly on the command line leaves it in your shell history. Only do this for testing.
